items.title: The Open Anatomy
items.summary: A field note that treats existing open-source projects as replaceable technical organs for a local, inspectable Cyberdelic OS, including Community Notes as a reference for helpfulness across differing perspectives.
questions: Which existing open-source organs can be borrowed without inheriting the surrounding platform's physics?
How can a system remain inspectable while its technical components stay replaceable?

items.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs
items.summary: A field note about large-group inquiry, disagreement, collective sensemaking, and the durable artifacts that can preserve sources, alternatives, ratification, and unresolved questions.
questions: How can a gathering reveal shared structure without making consensus the measure of truth?
What should remain visible when a complex disagreement becomes a durable public object?

evidence.locator: Field Note 25: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

items.title: The Living Librarian
items.summary: The conceptual origin of a library that tends meanings and relations around unchanged works, while keeping machine interpretation visibly situated, revisable, and distinct from fact.
questions: How can an archive learn better placement without harvesting its visitors?
How can changing relations gather around exact, unchanged works?

related.title: The Garden and the Living Map

items.title: The Plate and the Pull
items.summary: A proposal for durable generative publication in which an authorized edition can end while its algorithm, lineage, and capacity for independent reconstruction remain public.
questions: What must travel with a generative work for it to survive the disappearance of its first venue?
Can an edition end while its public algorithm remains copyable and renderable?

related.title: Open Container Initiative Image Format Specification

evidence.locator: A Press, Not a Platform; The Edition Ends. The Plate Remains.

items.title: Community Notes
items.summary: An open-source context system whose public ranking method looks for notes found helpful by contributors with differing prior rating patterns, producing one global status rather than personalized results.
questions: Which kinds of disagreement remain invisible when perspective is inferred from rating patterns?
What must remain visible beyond one global helpfulness status?

related.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

items.title: Polis
items.summary: An open-source platform for large-group sensemaking through participant statements, agree, disagree, or pass responses, and statistical mapping of opinion space.
questions: How can a gathering reveal agreement without erasing important forms of disagreement?

related.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

items.title: Art Blocks
items.summary: An on-chain generative-art protocol whose documented architecture offers a technical precedent for storing scripts, deterministic token hashes, and dependencies so works can be reconstructed beyond one service.
questions: Which infrastructure-independent techniques can inform a durable press without importing marketplace assumptions?

items.title: Web Archive Collection Zipped (WACZ)
items.summary: A portable web-archive packaging specification that carries recorded resources, indexes, entry pages, contextual metadata, and file fixity for static hosting and browser replay.
questions: Could a generative plate carry a similarly portable manifest while preserving its own execution and lineage model?

items.title: Open Container Initiative Image Format Specification
items.summary: A content-addressed image format that separates runnable filesystem content, execution configuration, and platform variants while binding referenced bytes through typed, sized, and verifiable descriptors.
questions: Could a generative plate distinguish immutable work content from replaceable reader and runtime configuration?
How much of an execution environment must travel for independent reconstruction?

items.title: WebAssembly Core Specification
items.summary: A portable low-level code format that defines module computation, validation, imports, and exports while requiring a separate embedder to supply environmental capabilities and initiate execution.
questions: Could a generative plate declare a small capability contract while allowing its reader to be replaced?
What remains outside portable computation when the intended encounter includes rendering, timing, fonts, colour, and randomness?
